take_homes: The agent proposes and I approve. Plan first, then files, with sources cited so I can check it. That is how I would pitch it to the board.
It is plain files in a folder: no database, no paid tier, and the model can be swapped. So the thing we build is ours and is not a licence.
Knowledge that sits in people's heads has to be written down first. That is the real work, not the tool.

monday.move: Ask the controller to try the month-end variance commentary with an agent once, on non-sensitive numbers, proposal-only, citing the files it used
monday.when: Monday, after I have asked IT whether the tool is approved for finance data
monday.stop_condition: IT says no, or the commentary has uncited claims or wrong figures
monday.blocker: IT has not approved the tool for finance data

misconception.why: The memory is a folder of our own files and survives a change of model, so the value sits with us and not with a licence. But no cost or payback appeared all day, so I only half believe it.

one_line: Sensible method: plan first, cite sources, plain files that stay ours. But it never gave me a price per month or a payback, and I wouldn't send my team to the styling bit or the 40 minutes of reading.
